meta.title: JARVIS — Homelab AI Cluster
meta.description: JARVIS — a private 19-node Kubernetes homelab: declarative GitOps infrastructure, multi-tier local AI inference, vision tracking, and zero-trust network segmentation.

hero.description: A 19-node Kubernetes homelab that thinks, sees, and listens at home — run entirely declaratively, with multi-tier local AI inference and zero-trust network segmentation.

goLive.title: Go-Live Countdown
goLive.description: Planned production start of the entire cluster — from bare-metal bootstrap to the speaking assistant.

systemMap.title: The Entire Toolchain at a Glance
systemMap.description: JARVIS as the hub across six domains — from GitOps and AI inference to security, voice & vision, and observability.

features.title: What JARVIS Does
features.description: From bare-metal node to speaking assistant — every capability runs on its own network, declaratively managed and versioned.

items.title: GitOps Infrastructure
items.description: A Git monorepo as the single source of truth. Ansible for the node layer, FluxCD for cluster state — every change is a reviewable commit, every drift is reconciled automatically.

items.title: 19-Node Bare-Metal Cluster
items.description: Raspberry Pi 5s, an ODROID-H5, and a GPU workstation combined into a K3s cluster — from edge device to inference hardware, all self-hosted, no cloud VMs.

items.title: Multi-Tier Local AI Inference
items.description: Requests are routed across staged hardware tiers — from NPU edge devices for instant short answers to a GPU workstation for complex reasoning. Cloud serves only as a tightly limited fallback.

items.title: Vision Tracker
items.description: Active person recognition with camera tracking (pan/tilt/zoom). Processing stays entirely in-cluster; only embeddings of enrolled people are stored — never raw images, no cloud path.

items.title: Voice Assistant & HUD
items.description: Wake-word detection, speech output, and a heads-up display showing identity and status in real time — including personalized greetings and presence-triggered automations.

items.title: Zero-Trust Network Segmentation
items.description: Default-deny network policies per workload namespace, encrypted node-to-node traffic, and an explicit, versioned allow-set instead of implicit reachability.

items.title: Security & Compliance
items.description: Controls aligned with ISO 27001, NIS-2, and CIS: secrets stored encrypted only, full API audit logging, runtime threat detection, and automated image scanning.

items.title: Automated Version Governance
items.description: Dependencies and chart versions are continuously checked and proposed as reviewable pull requests — no silent 'latest', every change visible and traceable.

items.title: Backup, DR & Observability
items.description: Tested backup and restore paths for the entire cluster, continuous monitoring, and dashboards across nodes, workloads, and network.

items.title: Home Automation
items.description: Integration with smart-home devices on the local network and presence-driven automations, orchestrated from the same platform as the AI and voice services.

pipeline.title: Fully Declarative Rollout

deepDive.title: How the Pieces Work Together
deepDive.description: Four building blocks explained more closely — no code, no internal configuration, just the underlying principle.

items.title: Vision Tracker & Logitech MeetUp
items.body: The Logitech MeetUp is a conference camera with motorized pan/tilt/zoom, controlled over the open UVC standard. One pod in the cluster owns the camera exclusively and handles two jobs at once: face detection on every frame (YuNet, CPU-based) and, for enrolled people, an embedding match (SFace) against a vector database (Qdrant). Once a known person is recognized, a simple controller with a dead zone and a speed limit keeps the camera pointed at them. The feed is also exposed as a stream for the heads-up display. Only embeddings of enrolled people are ever stored — never raw images, never a cloud call; unknown faces are counted but not tracked.

items.title: ZeroClaw — the Agent Framework
items.body: ZeroClaw orchestrates requests across the AI model tiers and equips them with tools (tool-calling) — access to smart-home devices, Vision-Tracker data, or n8n workflows. Unlike a single model reply, an agent can plan in multiple steps: check status, decide, act. The model chosen for tool-calling is continuously benchmarked against alternatives before a version goes into production.

items.title: n8n — Automation Without Code
items.body: n8n wires the JARVIS services together into automations. When the Vision Tracker recognizes someone present, n8n builds context for the voice assistant, including a personalized greeting and lighting control. It also evaluates power-consumption data and runs recurring checks like backup status. Workflows are versioned as JSON in the same Git repository as the rest of the infrastructure.

items.title: The Kubernetes Cluster (K3s)
items.body: K3s is a lightweight Kubernetes distribution built for edge and ARM hardware. Three nodes form the control plane, the rest run as workers. FluxCD reconciles cluster state against a Git repository every 10 minutes — any manual change gets reverted on the next pass. Longhorn handles replicated storage across nodes, Cilium the network including encryption. The entire state is reproducible from a single repository at any time.

power.title: Estimated Power Consumption
power.description: An approximation based on the rated power draw of the hardware in use — not measured values, but a sense of the order of magnitude.
power.wolBody: The GPU workstation (HP Z840), at 300+ W peak, is by far the single biggest consumer in the cluster — but it's only needed for the more demanding inference tier. An autosuspend mechanism puts it to sleep after a period without requests; a Wake-on-LAN magic packet wakes it specifically when a request needs that tier. That cuts its contribution to continuous consumption down to a small time-weighted fraction, without giving up on-demand GPU power.
